desc: Ideation: identify that one nums element can cover multiple targets via common multiple (LCM), and that naive partition DP is wrong because it may reuse the same element for disjoint subsets (counterexample nums=[5], target=[4,6]).
Design correct approach: per-element subset DP over masks, O(n · 3^m) ≈ 4·10^6 operations, feasible.
Implement solution: lcm[mask] precompute, per-element costs ceil(x/L)*L - x, mask DP with per-element snapshot to enforce single-use, return dp[full].

Verify against examples ([1,2,3],[4]→1; [8,4],[10,5]→2; [7,9,10],[7]→0) and the counterexample (nums=[5], target=[4,6]→7), plus edge cases (answer 0, huge LCM via Python big ints, duplicate targets, single element covering all targets).
